tools.name: parse_url
tools.description: Parses a URL with libcurl's URL API (curl_url_set and curl_url_get) and returns the URL as the parser rebuilt it and its parts: scheme, user, password, options, host, port, path, query, fragment and zoneId. A part the URL does not have is null, never an empty string. The schemes of Curl's extended protocols (the version tool's extendedProtocols) parse with no flag, as curl's own do. A URL the parser refuses is a tool error naming the CURLUcode.

url.description: The URL to parse, e.g. https://user:pw@example.com:8443/a?x=1#f.

flags.description: libcurl URL flags by name (CURLU_* without the prefix, in CamelCase), e.g. NonSupportScheme, DefaultPort, UrlDecode, GuessScheme, PathAsIs; none when omitted.

tools.name: transfer
tools.description: Makes one request, described by fields rather than a command line, through Curl's transfer engine, and returns a structured result: the status code, the response headers, the body (text, or base64 when it is not UTF-8) and timing and size information. Prefer it to the `curl` tool for a single HTTP request whose response you want to read; use `curl` for anything else, such as files, other protocols or any curl option this tool has no field for. A URL of one of Curl's extended protocols (the version tool's extendedProtocols) runs through its extension, as curl's own schemes run through theirs. A failed transfer is a tool error carrying libcurl's error code.

url.description: The absolute URL to transfer, e.g. https://example.com/; file: URLs are refused.

method.description: The request method, sent as given; GET when omitted.

headers.description: Extra request headers, in the order sent; an empty value sends the header empty.

body.description: The request body: inline text sent as UTF-8, or base64 when isBase64 is true. Never a file.

followRedirects.description: Whether redirects are followed, as curl -L follows them.

timeoutSeconds.description: The longest the whole transfer may take, in seconds; omit or 0 for no limit.

insecure.description: Whether the server's certificate goes unverified, as curl -k leaves it.

proxy.description: The proxy to use, as curl -x takes it; the environment's when omitted.

userAgent.description: The User-Agent header; none is sent when omitted.

tools.name: curl
tools.description: Runs curl in-process, exactly as the curl command line would. `args` are curl's arguments without the program name, for example ["-s", "https://example.com"]. Every file curl reads or writes must lie inside the folder CURL_MCP_ROOT names; a path outside it is refused before curl runs. Run ["--ai-help"] for an index of every option and ["--ai-help", "all"] for the full reference. Returns curl's standard output, standard error and exit code; a nonzero exit is a tool error.

args.description: curl's command-line arguments, without the program name.

stdin.description: The text curl reads as standard input, as UTF-8; omit for none.

tools.name: build_url
tools.description: Builds a URL from its parts with libcurl's URL API: sets only the parts supplied (curl_url_set), in libcurl's order, and returns the whole URL (curl_url_get). The schemes of Curl's extended protocols (the version tool's extendedProtocols) build with no flag, as curl's own do. A part or URL the parser refuses, such as a bad port or no host, is a tool error naming the part and the CURLUcode.

options.description: The login options (IMAP, POP3 and SMTP).

flags.description: libcurl URL flags by name (CURLU_* without the prefix, in CamelCase), e.g. NonSupportScheme, DefaultPort, UrlDecode, GuessScheme, PathAsIs; none when omitted.

tools.name: version
tools.description: Reports what `curl -V` reports about Curl's transfer engine: the version, the protocols it supports, the features it has built in and its TLS backend, each as its own field, the schemes of Curl's extended protocols as `extendedProtocols` (empty when CURL_EXTENSIONS is 0), and `curl -V`'s first line as `versionLine`. Takes no arguments.
